findings.title: Constructor validates grantType twice, never validates rawTokenId
findings.body: AccessTokenContext constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) twice and never checks rawTokenId, despite the second message saying 'Null rawTokenId not allowed'. A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted and later produces an id like 'onrtac:null' or an NPE in encodeTokenId / getRawTokenId consumers.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher is inverted and uses wrong substring
findings.body: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId the check is `if (items[0].substring(3,5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. It returns false when the shortcut matches and true when it does not, so tests pass for wrong grants and fail for correct ones. The offsets are also wrong: the encoded prefix is 6 chars (session 0-2, token-type 2-4, grant 4-6), so the grant shortcut must be substring(4,6), not substring(3,5).

findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks all existing custom grant factories
findings.body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory adds abstract String getShortcut() with no default implementation. Any third-party provider implementing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory will fail to compile and existing deployed providers will throw AbstractMethodError when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory calls getShortcut() in postInit. It should have a default method or fallback.

findings.title: Duplicate shortcut/ID validation by map-size comparison is ineffective
findings.body: postInit detects duplicate grant IDs or shortcuts by comparing grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size(). If two grants collide on both maps consistently, or one overwrites the other in both maps, sizes stay equal and the collision is missed, silently mapping a shortcut to the wrong grant. If they collide on only one side the error message is cryptic. Explicit duplicate checks on put are required.

findings.title: Decoding a token id throws on any unexpected format instead of falling back
findings.body: getTokenContextFromTokenId throws IllegalArgumentException when the prefix before ':' is not exactly 6 chars or contains an unknown shortcut. Any token whose id contains ':' for other reasons, or was issued by a custom grant with a shortcut longer than 2 chars, or after a grant is undeployed, will cause an exception to bubble to callers (e.g. introspection/userinfo/session lookup) instead of returning UNKNOWN context like the no-colon legacy path does. This turns malformed or forward-compatible tokens into 500 errors.

findings.title: Unchecked cast of all OAuth2GrantType factories can cause ClassCastException
findings.body: postInit and getGrantTypeByShortcut cast every OAuth2GrantType provider factory to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory. A custom OAuth2GrantType provider whose factory does not implement the new sub-interface will cause a ClassCastException at server startup or on first decode, breaking boot. Code should use instanceof filtering or lookup.
